15.7 Polyprotic Acids

We emphasize two important points at the outset:

1. The [H3O1] in the two ionization equilibria are one and the same. 2. Ka2 is invariably smaller than Ka1 because the negative charge left behind by the loss of a hydrogen ion in the first ionization causes the second hydrogen ion to be more tightly bound.
